title: landolphia nitidula
intro: Landolphia nitidula, commonly known as the African forest yew, is a plant species in the Apocynaceae family. It is a woody climber that has been traditionally used in various cultures for its medicinal properties. The health benefits of Landolphia nitidula include its use in treating fever, rheumatism, and skin conditions, among others. The bioactive constituents of this plant include alkaloids, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions such as anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, which help to reduce pain, inflammation, and oxidative stress.
